name: Circuit de la Sarthe
layout: 24 Hours of Le Mans circuit (2018+ configuration, Bugatti + public roads)

sources.geometry: OpenStreetMap route=raceway relation 2126739 "Circuit des 24 Heures du Mans" (distance 13.626) member ways (raceway + public roads D338/D140/D139), start-finish node 3599294865; Overpass API, (c) OSM contributors ODbL
sources.width: Published/typical section widths (approximate): ~15 m start-finish straight, ~12 m permanent Bugatti/Porsche sections, ~10-11 m Hunaudières (D338) and chicanes, ~9.5 m Route du Golf/Arnage (D140/D139). Aerial edge-line measurement on IGN ORTHO was tried but public-road lane markings make it unreliable.
sources.elevation: IGN RGE ALTI 1 m via Geoplateforme altimetry REST https://data.geopf.fr/altimetrie/1.0/calcul/alti/rest/elevation.json (resource ign_rge_alti_wld, batched), robust median + ~15 m smoothing; DTM dips at bridges (track over roads/streams) filled by linear interpolation
sources.camber: Crossfall from RGE ALTI 1 m samples at both track edges (1.2 m inset), trackkit.profile_from_samples; public-road crown/camber included as measured
sources.pit: OSM relation 2126739 pit_lane members (Pit Entry before the Ford chicanes, Pit Exit after Courbe Dunlop)
sources.trim: Very long straights (Hunaudieres, Mulsanne-Indianapolis, pit straight): lowest-drag configuration of the season, below Monza
sources.pitLimit: ACO/FIA WEC 24 Hours of Le Mans sporting regulations: pit lane speed limit 60 km/h
sources.pitLoss: Not set: no reliable published WEC pit-loss figure found

notes: Clockwise. No official FIA turn numbers are in common use at Le Mans; corners are the named ACO corners numbered sequentially in race order. RGE ALTI 1 m in Sarthe is the IGN 1 m terrain model (LiDAR/correlation mix).
